mission: Reconstruct archaeologically attested stages of the Osirian Khoiak reassembly/burial process so manufactured ritual substitutes can be distinguished from any hypothetical biological relic.

core_result.interpretation: The material record now preserves different physical stages of the same broad ritual technology at independent sites. This substantially strengthens the ritual-substitute model and creates concrete object-level comparison controls for Mendes CG53469 and other body-part traditions.

coptos_manufacture_node.type: pink-granite Osirian ritual basin / cuve osirienne
coptos_manufacture_node.discovery: accidentally uncovered by sebakhin workers at Coptos/Qift in 1904 and transferred to the Cairo Museum
coptos_manufacture_node.primary_scholarly_anchor: Jean Yoyotte, EPHE annual report 1977-1978, pp. 163-172
coptos_manufacture_node.modern_full_publication: François René Herbin and Christian Leitz, Le rituel de la Maison de Chentayt: le linceul MMA 31.9.8 et la cuve osirienne de Coptos Caire JE 37516, 2022
secure_facts: Yoyotte explicitly rejects the earlier royal-sarcophagus interpretation based on dimensions, cavity proportions and wall decoration
decorative scenes show Harsiese and his son performing rites before Osiris-Khentamenti and Shentayt of Abydos/Busiris
the monument preserves ritual texts important for Osiris cult practice
coptos_manufacture_node.outreach: Targeted inquiry sent 2026-09-03 to Christian Leitz regarding physical function, drains/openings, wear/residues, current custody and relation to Dendera and Thonis SCA0459.

giza_annual_burial_node.site: Ptolemaic Osirian cemetery discovered during 1994 Ring Road excavations, western Giza plateau, approximately 2.5 km south of the Sphinx
giza_annual_burial_node.excavation: under supervision cited by Abdelrahman & Eissa as Zahi Hawass, Ehab Amer and Mohamed Yossef
giza_annual_burial_node.architecture: square shafts 80-100 cm deep with small western burial chamber containing ~50 cm wooden coffin
giza_annual_burial_node.ritual_product: clay-and-wheat Osiris statuette wrapped in bandages; some examples reportedly preserved remains of erect phallus

five_core_coffins.source: Amal Samuel 2010 unpublished Cairo University PhD as summarized/reproduced by Abdelrahman & Eissa 2022

503.type: foot-side fragment of coffin containing clay Osiris statuette
503.inscription: Ptolemaic royal name + Sokar-Osiris + dynastic ancestors

giza_annual_burial_node.open_gate: Recover original 1994 SCA tomb-by-tomb association, current inventory numbers for 501/1-501/5 and associated objects, location of the four clay balls, material analyses and any surviving ithyphallic specimen.
giza_annual_burial_node.outreach: Targeted inquiry sent 2026-09-03 to Abdelrahman Ali Abdelrahman and Maher Eissa.

oxyrhynchos_annual_catacomb_node.mission: University of Barcelona / Egyptian archaeological mission
official_site_facts: wall niches used for annual burial of the previous year's earthen Osiris statuette
hieratic niche inscriptions date individual burials from Ptolemy VI through the joint reign of Ptolemy X Soter II and Cleopatra III
one gallery contains a prone Osiris statue more than three metres long
oxyrhynchos_annual_catacomb_node.archaeological_product: A complete statuette was reportedly found in a niche; published description gives Nile mud mixed with bitumen and barley grains, wrapped in fine linen. Other degraded examples include ithyphallic forms and funerary equipment.

ritual_protection_system.evidence: Recent scholarship citing Mascort, Oxyrhynchos IV vol. II pp. 242-250 states that protective vessels each contained a magical bulla intended to guard Osiris and repel Seth/hostile forces.
ritual_protection_system.catalogue: Maite Mascort, Oxyrhynchos IV: L'Osireion d'Oxirrinc, vol. II, 2018/2019, 256 pp.; catalogue of archaeological and ritual materials from inside and outside the Osireion
ritual_protection_system.passport_gap: individual excavation/catalogue numbers for the vessels/bullae and the complete in-situ annual Osiris burial remain to be extracted

oxyrhynchos_annual_catacomb_node.outreach: Targeted inquiry sent 2026-09-03 to excavation co-director Esther Pons requesting individual object numbers, context, sealed-status and residue/material data.

triangulation.COPTOS: physical ritual basin and textual manufacture technology
triangulation.GIZA: annual individual shaft burials with coffins, manufactured Osiris bodies and associated protection objects
triangulation.OXYRHYNCHOS: year-by-year inscribed catacomb sequence with manufactured Osiris bodies and magical protective equipment
triangulation.THONIS_HERACLEION_parallel: SCA0459 garden tank plus ritual ladles/situlae/strainers provides a fourth independent equipment-level control
triangulation.consequence: Manufacture, embodiment, protection, annual burial and eventual replacement are archaeologically observable processes. Therefore later texts or labels calling such products 'relics', 'parts' or Osiris bodies cannot by themselves establish biological identity.

impact_on_missing_parts_hunt.rule: Every candidate body part must now be tested against the ritual-substitute pipeline before promotion.
required_discriminator: closed archaeological context or continuous provenance
identity-bearing inscription, residue, anatomy or custody invariant
impact_on_missing_parts_hunt.mendes_status: Mendes CG53469/JE35425 and the stamped-gold djed remain priority because their source-bound protected human-body context differs structurally from annual corn-mummy ritual manufacture; this difference must be tested rather than erased.

canonical_seal: THE ANCIENTS LEFT THE RECIPE, THE BASIN, THE MANUFACTURED BODY, THE PROTECTIVE PACKAGE, THE ANNUAL GRAVE AND THE DATE. THAT EXPLAINS MANY 'PIECES OF OSIRIS' BEFORE WE EVER NEED A BIOLOGICAL RELIC HYPOTHESIS.
